conventions.convention: Q=Ω×(0,T]; its parabolic boundary is (closure Ω×{0})∪(boundary Ω×[0,T]). The spatially interior final face is excluded. C^{2,1} requires continuous spatial derivatives through order two and one time derivative; at T the time derivative is left-sided. No boundary regularity is implicit.

Heat balls are closed superlevel sets with the top point adjoined. Their bottom depth is r²/(4π), whose slice is a singleton. Sphere integration in spatial dimension one counts the two points; endpoint slices do not affect the time integral.

Duhamel integrals take values in Lp classes and are Bochner integrals. Strong measurability is required for L1-in-time forcing, including p=∞; weak measurability alone is insufficient. Classical forcing is bounded, jointly continuous and uniformly spatially Hölder. Mild initial-trace continuity is asserted for finite p.
Gaussian growth bounds use constants uniform on the entire closed finite-time strip, not constants depending on time.
Complex time uses the principal logarithm on Sθ={z≠0:|arg z|<θ}, with 0<θ<π/2. Holomorphy is in operator norm at positive complex times for all p; C0 continuity at the vertex is restricted to p<∞.
The interval backward map is defined on terminal profiles of C^{4,2} Dirichlet solutions. Sine modes have indices k≥1 and squared L² norm π/2.

Elliptic forms and L² pairings are linear in the first slot and conjugate-linear in the second. The adjoint form is a*(u,v)=conjugate(a(v,u)); measurable drift coefficients make the formal adjoint distributional, not necessarily a function.

H¹₀ is the Sobolev closure of compactly supported smooth functions. The symmetric operator has b=0, Hermitian principal coefficients and real c. Its operator domain consists of form-domain elements with an L² representer; measurable coefficients do not imply Cc∞⊂D(L). Dirichlet compactness needs boundedness but no boundary regularity.

Elliptic eigenvalues are indexed from j=1, listed nondecreasingly with geometric multiplicity, and need not be positive when c is negative. Compactness and Fredholm results carry AC; the Sobolev and Hilbert interfaces carry CC.
The elliptic inverse convention is Rz=(L̃−z)⁻¹, the negative of the library resolvent (z−L̃)⁻¹. Real operators are complexified before complex spectrum and resolvent statements.

The positive mean-zero Neumann level requires a nonempty bounded connected W^{1,2}-extension domain. The full H¹ Neumann problem retains the constant zero mode; disconnected domains retain componentwise constants.

For N≥1 the forward DFT has negative phase and factor N⁻¹ᐟ²; the inverse has positive phase with the same factor. Both sides use counting inner products without 1/N. Cyclic convolution is unnormalised, so its unitary transform law carries √N.

FFT levels start at m=0, length one. The recursion computes the unnormalised transform at N=2^m. Its operation model counts one twiddle multiplication and one addition per output at every nonbase level, excluding twiddle evaluation, indexing, memory, bit complexity and stability.

load_bearing.statement: Assume CC. On an open Ω, take the uniformly elliptic bounded measurable form with b=0, Hermitian principal coefficients and real c. Define D(L)={u∈H¹₀: there exists f∈L² with a(u,v)=(f,v) for every v∈H¹₀}, and Lu=f. Density of H¹₀ in L² makes f unique. D(L) contains the range of each admissible shifted solution operator; Cc∞⊂D(L) is not asserted.

Assume CC. For the stated uniformly elliptic form on an open Ω, fix μ≥β=θ/2+nMb²/(2θ)+Mc. Kμf is the unique u∈H¹₀ satisfying aμ(u,v)=(f,v) for every v∈H¹₀, where aμ=a+μ(·,·)L². Kμ is linear L²→H¹₀ and ||Kμf||H¹₀≤(2/θ)||f||L². Its L² realization uses the inclusion; no boundedness or boundary regularity is needed for this definition.

For n≥1, nonempty bounded open Ω and T>0, Q=Ω×(0,T], closure Q=closure Ω×[0,T], and boundary_p Q=(closure Ω×{0})∪(boundary Ω×[0,T]). C^{2,1}(closure Q) requires continuity and continuous extensions of the spatial derivatives through order two and the first time derivative, interpreted from the left at T.

Assume AC and CC. In the stated symmetric case on nonempty bounded open Ω, fix μ≥β. There are real λ1≤λ2≤…→+∞, repeated with finite multiplicity, and an L² orthonormal basis ej∈H¹₀ with a(ej,v)=λj(ej,v) for all v∈H¹₀. They satisfy λj=νj⁻¹−μ for positive eigenvalues νj↓0 of Kμ. Every weak eigenvalue occurs, distinct eigenspaces are orthogonal, λj>−μ, and a(u,u)≥−β||u||²L² for u∈H¹₀.

For N≥1 and every complex function f on Z/NZ, (F_Nf)(k)=N⁻¹ᐟ²∑_{x=0}^{N−1}f([x])exp(−2πikx/N). This is periodic in the integer k, hence defines a function on Z/NZ, and F_N is linear. Invertibility, isometry and the convolution law are proved separately.
Let Q=Ω×(0,T] be the stated bounded parabolic cylinder, and let u∈C^{2,1}(closure Q) satisfy u_t−Δu≤0 in Q. Then max_{closure Q}u=max_{boundary_p Q}u.

Assume CC. For u∈C^{2,1} on a neighbourhood of the closed heat ball E_r(t,x), with f=u_t−Δu, u(x,t) equals the volume integral of (Γ(x−y,t−s)−r⁻ⁿ)f over E plus (1/(2rⁿ)) times the time integral of ρ_n(t−s)/(t−s) times the sphere integral of u on |y−x|=ρ_n(t−s). Both integrals converge absolutely; for n=1 sphere integration sums two points.

Assume CC. Bounded jointly continuous uniformly spatially γ-Hölder forcing, 0<γ≤1, has a scalar heat potential classical in positive time, with u_t−Δu=f and zero initial data. For 1≤p<∞ and f∈C([0,T];Lp), Df is continuous, vanishes initially and satisfies Df(t)=H_{t−s}Df(s)+∫_s^tH_{t−τ}f(τ)dτ for 0<s<t≤T; every continuous zero-data curve satisfying this relation equals Df. Classical solutions with the forcing of the classical clause are unique in the stated Gaussian growth class.

Assume AC and CC. For the symmetric elliptic eigenbasis on nonempty bounded open Ω and μ≥β, every u∈H¹₀ has its L² coefficient series converging in H¹₀, with aμ(u,u)=∑(λj+μ)|(u,ej)|². Every f∈L² has its expansion and Parseval identity in L². Consequently a(u,u)=∑λj|(u,ej)|², absolutely convergently.

Assume AC and CC. For the stated divergence-form problem on bounded open Ω with L² data, exactly one alternative holds: the homogeneous kernel is zero and every datum has a unique H¹₀ solution; or the primal and adjoint homogeneous spaces are nonzero finite-dimensional spaces of equal dimension, solvability is equivalent to L² orthogonality of the datum to the adjoint kernel, and each nonempty solution set is an affine translate of the primal kernel. H⁻¹ data are not treated.

For M≥1, N=2M and any input f on Z/NZ, its even and odd parts on Z/MZ are e(r)=f(2r), o(r)=f(2r+1). Their index maps are well-defined injections with disjoint exhaustive images. For all integer k, Xk(f)=Xk(e)+exp(−2πik/N)Xk(o) and X_{k+M}(f)=Xk(e)−exp(−2πik/N)Xk(o), with the shorter transforms extended periodically.

concerns.concern: The page says, “On the square the eigenvalue 5 has a two-dimensional eigenspace”. Its companion cex-elliptic-eigenvalues-need-not-be-simple, Counterexample 2.1–3.1, establishes dimension at least two, not an upper bound. Exact multiplicity two is true for this square, but the summary strengthens the supplied witness; either retain “at least” or supply the exact-multiplicity argument.

seams_checked.note: Opened the form, H⁻¹, coefficient, weak-solution, H¹-Hilbert, Lax–Milgram and inverse-bound suppliers. The consumers use bounded conjugate-linear datum functionals under CC, preserve the linear-first convention, and derive shifted coercivity locally rather than importing the smallness theorem beyond its hypotheses.

Conceptual page prerequisite only: no owned finite-sum proof imports an item from this page. The finite-Haar example agrees with F_N=√N times the probability-Haar transform. Separate source-page defect for group j: its prose says “norm continuity of translations in every Lp”, while lem-lca-translations-and-normalised-local-approximate-identities explicitly assumes 1≤p<∞. On R, translations of the half-line indicator have L∞ difference norm one for every nonzero shift. The supplier item itself is correctly restricted. Routing limitation: tools/step7-scope.mjs accepts cross-group alerts only for item owners, so this page-only finding is recorded here instead of falsely attributing it to the valid lemma.

Opened the page, biduality, LCA Plancherel and compact/discrete special-case statements. This is a conceptual prerequisite; the owned character orthogonality, inversion and FFT proofs are independent finite computations. They neither import general biduality without AC/DC nor confuse compatible Haar weights with counting weights.

Opened thm-viscous-scalar-cauchy-problem-with-smooth-data-has-a-global-classical-solution. Its F4 and Proof 5.1 use the cylinder's initial/lateral boundary distinction. The viscous drift barrier argument is proved locally, rather than cited as a consequence of the drift-free maximum theorem; positive maxima occur at positive times where the derivatives exist.

Opened the lattice/sampling page and checked its companion inventory for owned-item references. This is a contextual prerequisite with no DFT/FFT item-level proof use. Its Euclidean 2π-normalised transform is stated separately; the finite counting normalisation and radix-two operation bound are not transferred to lattice or Shannon claims.

Opened the interior H² theorem, normal-derivative recovery lemma, uniqueness-based global estimate and smooth-eigenfunction corollary. Their smooth-test density uses preserve CC and localise L² where necessary. The global estimate uses the actual L²→H¹₀ bounded inverse under a trivial kernel and carries AC/CC. The eigenfunction corollary imports only the weak eigenidentity and supplies smoothness through later regularity hypotheses.

Opened thm-finite-dft-support-product-uncertainty and its delta/constant and singleton companions. The theorem quotes the counting pairing, negative-phase N⁻¹ᐟ² transform and Parseval faithfully; it establishes nonempty transformed support using Parseval, not the DFT Definition alone. The constant example applies character orthogonality with parameters 0,k, giving the required negative phase. All three preserve the N=1 boundary case.
